title: IBM releases Granite Speech 5.0 for transcription, translation, and on-device speed
friendlyTitle: IBM releases speech models you can run yourself
summary: IBM has published granite-speech-5.0-2b, an Apache-2.0 speech model that transcribes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, and translates to and from English in those languages, plus English to Italian and Mandarin. It adds language-name prompting and keyword lists of up to 2,000 terms. IBM also updated a 470-million-parameter Turbo CTC model for multilingual on-device transcription, and updated granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus for speaker labels and timestamps. IBM says the 2B model's average English word-error rate was 5.06% on a public short-form set, an unofficial comparison as of 15 October.
friendlySummary: IBM has published a new speech model, granite-speech-5.0-2b, under the Apache 2.0 licence. It turns speech into text in English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese. It can translate to and from English in those languages, and from English into Italian and Mandarin. You can name the language in the prompt, and give it a list of up to 2,000 special words. IBM also updated a smaller model, about 470 million parameters, for fast transcription on a device, now in several languages. A third update is better at saying who spoke, and when. IBM says the 2B model's average English error rate was 5.06% on a public set of short clips. That comparison is IBM's own, and it is unofficial, as of 15 October.
whyItMatters: A meeting note that has to stay on the laptop can use the small model. A transcript that has to catch product names can use the 2B model and a keyword list. The accuracy number is IBM's. The licence is the practical part: Apache 2.0, with support in Transformers, vLLM, llama.cpp, and MLX.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If a meeting note has to stay on the laptop, the small model is the one to try. If a transcript has to catch product names, the 2B model can take a word list. The accuracy number is IBM's. The useful part is the licence: Apache 2.0, and it works with common tools for running models, including on Apple silicon.
